name: Ricardo Cunha
tagline: I build AI products and the platforms that run them.
bio: Principal Architect in Brazil, working remotely with U.S. companies. I started in 2005 on desktop automation for the Brazilian post office, moved through insurance, fintech and payments, and now build AI products: RAG and agent workflows that turn messy regulatory text into structured data, and the Go services, data pipelines and Kubernetes platforms underneath them. I work spec-first, so that what an agent builds can be checked against what was asked.
highlights: Agent workflows (Python, LangChain/LangGraph, RAG) that cut manual collection of EV incentive data by 90%, with human review kept for validation
Event-driven EV fleet platform for 300 enterprise customers and 6,000 vehicles: 360K API calls a day, 8M+ telemetry records a month, 20 TB of analytics data
Go REST/gRPC APIs with load times reduced by 60% through caching and a horizontally scalable rewrite
Multi-region AWS EKS disaster recovery that met the company SLA three years running
Defined the department's Spec-Driven Development workflow for AI-assisted engineering

projects.name: keelgw
projects.title: Keel Gateway
projects.pitch: Multi-tenant AI gateway that lets a small business govern how its people use AI: which models each member can reach, through which clients, and at what USD spend, all on the company's own provider accounts.
projects.details: A Go streaming proxy sits between Claude Code, Claude Cowork or Codex and the company's Anthropic, Bedrock or OpenAI accounts. Members sign in with a work account instead of handling API keys; quota is reserved before each request and settled from token usage. Remote MCP servers are filtered and logged at the gateway.
facts: About 0.6 ms median proxy overhead, measured locally against a mock provider
24 Prometheus alert rules, each with a runbook
Built spec-first with OpenSpec: 19 changes, 8 ADRs
projects.status: Runs end to end on a laptop (kind plus an AWS emulator). Not deployed to AWS yet.

projects.name: sportsvision
projects.title: SportsVision
projects.pitch: Turns football video into structured, evidence-backed offside decisions, and says so when it cannot make one.
projects.details: A Python perception plane (RF-DETR detection, ByteTrack tracking, team clustering, homography) feeds a deterministic Go rules engine. Every detected pass gets an offside line, a margin in metres and a confidence built from seven named terms; INCONCLUSIVE and REVIEW_REQUIRED are first-class outcomes.
facts: Five services over six queues, scaling from zero on queue depth
21 ADRs and JSON Schema contracts between Go and Python, checked for drift in CI
Apache-2.0, including every model it uses
projects.status: Full pipeline runs on a local Kubernetes cluster. No accuracy figure yet: there are no labelled clips, so thresholds are uncalibrated.
